channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan and Turkmenistan Sign Energy Cooperation Agreement in Ashgabat
item.description: The 7th session of the Kyrgyz-Turkmen intergovernmental commission on trade, economic, scientific, technical, and humanitarian cooperation was held in Ashgabat. Key discussions focused on expanding trade, economic, and energy partnerships, as well as transport and logistics. An agreement was signed between the National Electric Network of Kyrgyzstan and Turkmenistan Energy Corporation.

item.title: Canada Reports Significant Progress in Restoring Trade Relations with China
item.description: Canadian Prime Minister Justin Trudeau announced substantial progress in restoring trade relations and expanding economic cooperation with China. Canada has regained market access for over 90% of previously tariffed goods, with exports to China increasing by 20% this year, reaching $125 billion in bilateral trade.

item.title: Russia Attacks Kyiv Shortly After Summits with US and China
item.description: Russia launched an attack on Kyiv shortly after summits involving the US and China. The attack resulted in the death of a 26-year-old man and injured at least four others. One drone reportedly hit a building near the Netherlands embassy.

item.title: Uzbek President meets Turkish Vice President to strengthen strategic partnership
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev met with Turkish Vice President Cevdet Yılmaz to discuss strengthening the comprehensive strategic partnership between Uzbekistan and Turkey. Discussions focused on expanding trade, economic, and investment cooperation across various sectors, including industry, agriculture, construction, IT, tourism, transport, and energy.

item.title: Uzbekistan discusses legal capacity and legal competence of persons with disabilities
item.description: An expert roundtable in Tashkent focused on the legal capacity and competence of people with disabilities, examining research, national practices, and international experience to improve Uzbek legislation. The discussion centered on Article 12 of the UN Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities, emphasizing equal recognition before the law and ensuring support for independent decision-making.

item.title: Astana identifies over 150 violations in food price control since early 2026
item.description: Astana's price control commission has detected more than 150 violations in monitoring food prices since the beginning of 2026. The city's trade and consumer rights protection department is actively monitoring prices in various stores and markets, ensuring adherence to the 15% markup limit on socially significant food products.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Turkmenistan Plan to Resume Flights and Simplify Visa Regime
item.description: Uzbekistan and Turkmenistan are planning to resume air travel and simplify the visa regime, according to the Uzbek Ministry of Foreign Affairs. Discussions included transport links, border crossings, and visa-free travel for residents of border areas. Regular flights between Tashkent and Ashgabat were also considered, along with consular protection.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Implement Drug Testing for Government Officials
item.description: Kazakhstan has approved new rules for drug and psychotropic substance testing of civil servants, effective November 29. The rules outline observation of employee behavior by HR and supervisors, with specific signs like sudden behavioral changes or impaired coordination potentially leading to medical examination. Refusal to test will be documented.

item.title: Tajikistan Calls for Strengthening Regional Cooperation on Climate Change
item.description: At the COP31 conference, Tajikistan emphasized the need for enhanced regional and international cooperation to address climate change. The Committee for Environmental Protection highlighted climate challenges like glacier melt and water scarcity, stressing their impact on security and stability.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Canada Discuss New Avenues for Partnership and Investment
item.description: Uzbekistan's Foreign Minister Bakhtiyor Saidov met with Canadian Ambassador Christopher Duggan to explore expanding bilateral relations. Discussions focused on increasing trade, attracting Canadian investment and technology to Uzbekistan's priority sectors, and strengthening cooperation in education and tourism. Both sides expressed confidence in future collaboration.

item.title: WHO Reports Decline in Respiratory Infections and Measles Cases in Afghanistan
item.description: The World Health Organization (WHO) reported a decrease in acute respiratory infections and measles cases in Afghanistan during October. Respiratory infections saw a 3.8 percent decline, with 94,104 cases and 149 deaths recorded. Suspected measles cases dropped by 22.6 percent, with 1,152 cases and five related deaths reported.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Oman Strengthen Ties During President Mirziyoyev's State Visit
item.description: Uzbekistan and Oman are building on historical ties of mutual respect and shared values to foster strategic partnership. Recent years have seen increased business contacts, with 8 Omani-capitalized companies operating in Uzbekistan. The state visit by President Shavkat Mirziyoyev to Oman on November 16-17 aimed to deepen political dialogue and expand trade-economic cooperation, particularly in the transport and logistics sector.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Germany Host Seminar on Precision Agriculture and Climate-Resilient Farming
item.description: An international expert seminar on implementing precision agriculture and developing climate-resilient agriculture in Uzbekistan is taking place in Tashkent and Samarkand from November 16-20. Organized under the German-Uzbek Expert Dialogue Programme, the event focuses on efficient resource management, water conservation, soil fertility, and adapting agricultural production to climate change.

item.title: Kazakhstan's People's Council Discusses 25 Initiatives for Workers' Rights and Labor Relations
item.description: The People's Council of Kazakhstan, with support from the Pavlodar regional administration, held a meeting with representatives of the trade union movement. Discussions focused on social-labor policy, protecting workers' rights, and developing labor relations. The meeting resulted in 25 initiatives proposed to the People's Council to protect workers' interests and develop systemic solutions at the national level.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan National Bank Sets Currency Exchange Rates for November 20
item.description: The National Bank of Kyrgyzstan has announced official exchange rates for foreign currencies on November 20. The Euro has recovered, rising above 96 soms, while the US Dollar remains stable at 87.45 soms. The Russian Ruble and Kazakh Tenge have depreciated, and the Chinese Yuan has slightly strengthened.

item.title: Kazakhstan Plans to Invest 6.5 Trillion Tenge from National Fund for Infrastructure
item.description: Kazakhstan intends to allocate approximately 6.5 trillion tenge from its National Fund for the construction of schools, hospitals, and roads by the end of 2029. The 'People's Construction' program aims to develop infrastructure, addressing the growing needs due to a population increase of over 2 million in seven years.

item.title: Another Employee of Samruk-Kazyna Fund Detained in Corruption Case
item.description: Another employee of the Samruk-Kazyna Fund has been detained as part of a case involving the fund's leadership. The fund confirmed the detention of an employee from one of its departments, stating the investigation relates to their former activities and does not affect current duties. Details of the investigation and charges remain undisclosed.

item.title: Uzbekistan Reports Results of Anti-Corruption Efforts
item.description: Uzbekistan's Anti-Corruption Agency reported that 594 criminal, 160 administrative cases, and 4,604 disciplinary actions were taken against employees. Violations related to conflicts of interest and affiliation were identified in public procurement, totaling billions of Uzbek soums. Compliance control units prevented nearly 19,000 potential conflicts of interest.

item.title: Uzbek President Discusses Judo Team Preparation for Los Angeles Olympics with IJF Head
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev met with International Judo Federation (IJF) President Marius Vizer to discuss enhancing the national judo school and preparing young athletes. Tashkent is becoming a global judo center, hosting numerous international competitions. The discussion also covered organizing future tournaments and sports medicine cooperation.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Presents Approaches to Social Protection Against Climate Risks at COP31
item.description: Kyrgyzstan presented its strategies for social protection against climate change impacts at COP31 in Antalya, Turkey. The focus was on the care economy, women's and children's rights, and green job creation. The session highlighted the need to expand women's opportunities in STEM and ensure their potential is considered in climate and water resource policies.

item.title: Former Deputy Head of Bishkek Police Detained by National Security Committee
item.description: Syunali Amrakulov, former deputy head of Bishkek's police department for operational work, has been detained by the State Committee for National Security (GKNB) in connection with a contraband phone case. He was reportedly dismissed on October 27 due to the scandal. Three police officers, a border guard, a customs official, and one civilian are also detained.

item.title: Kazakh President Receives Speaker of Australian House of Representatives
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev met with Milton Dick, Speaker of the Australian House of Representatives and President of the Inter-Parliamentary Union. Tokayev congratulated Dick on his election and emphasized Kazakhstan's commitment to strengthening ties with the IPU. Both sides discussed parliamentary diplomacy, AI development, and Kazakh-Australian cooperation.

item.title: US authorities dismantle major drug cartel 'Los del Campo' in Puerto Rico
item.description: US federal authorities have conducted a large-scale operation in Puerto Rico against the 'Los del Campo' drug cartel. 55 members of the criminal group have been charged. The organization allegedly earned approximately $100 million from illegal drug trafficking between 2022 and 2026, with annual profits reaching up to $45 million.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan plans to establish 1,410 agro-clusters and 660 cooperatives by 2036
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Ministry of Agriculture has proposed a concept for the development of agro-industrial clusters for 2026-2036. The plan aims to create 1,410 clusters, 660 agricultural cooperatives, and hundreds of processing enterprises. By 2036, the volume of agricultural product processing is projected to reach 282 billion soms.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Turkey launch high-level business council to boost joint projects
item.description: Uzbekistan and Turkey have held their first high-level business council meeting, co-chaired by Saida Mirziyoyeva. The initiative aims to strengthen investment and business ties, remove administrative barriers for entrepreneurs, and provide comprehensive support for joint projects between the two nations.

item.title: Namangan Region Pursues Major Investment Projects, Including Airport Terminal and IT Park
item.description: Uzbekistan's President Mirziyoyev reviewed investment projects in Namangan, aiming to boost employment and income. The region expects $5.4 billion in foreign investment this year, with plans to reach $7-8 billion by 2027. Projects include a new airport terminal, industrial facilities, and a new IT Park.

item.title: Recycling Business Creates Jobs for 60 People in Maidan Wardak, Afghanistan
item.description: An entrepreneur has established a scrap collection and recycling business in Maidan Wardak province, creating jobs for approximately 60 people. The business collects and processes metal and plastic waste, supplying materials to factories and providing income amid economic hardship. Workers earn between 400 and 500 afghanis daily.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Marat Kozhayev Heads CIS Interparliamentary Assembly Political Commission
item.description: Kazakhstan's Kurultai deputy Marat Kozhayev was elected chairman of the CIS Interparliamentary Assembly's permanent commission on political issues and international cooperation. The decision was made at a meeting in Turkmenistan, where participants discussed regional security, counter-terrorism, and AI's role in combating threats. The commission also supported granting Turkmenistan observer status at the IPA CIS.

item.title: Trump, Xi, and Putin Sign Declaration on Peace and Reform
item.description: A brief joint document was signed by US President Donald Trump, Chinese President Xi Jinping, and Russian President Vladimir Putin following their meeting in Shenzhen. The declaration expresses commitment to reforming the UN, increasing oil product supplies, and warns against the International Criminal Court overstepping its bounds. The leaders also affirmed that there can be no winners in a nuclear war.

item.title: Uzbek President Meets with Head of International Judo Federation
item.description: The President of Uzbekistan met with the head of the International Judo Federation to discuss expanding cooperation in developing the national judo school and training young athletes. The meeting focused on strengthening the partnership between the federation and Uzbekistan's sports institutions.

item.title: Kazakh President Receives President of the Inter-Parliamentary Union
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev met with Milton Dick, President of the Inter-Parliamentary Union and Speaker of the Australian House of Representatives. Tokayev congratulated Dick on his election and expressed Kazakhstan's high regard for its cooperation with the IPU. They discussed parliamentary diplomacy, AI development, and Kazakhstan-Australia relations.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Customs Uncovers 4.35 Million Som Tax Evasion at Naryn SEZ
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Customs Service has identified violations of foreign raw material usage conditions at the Naryn Free Economic Zone (SEZ). Over 575 tons of raw materials under customs control could not be accounted for, resulting in unpaid duties totaling 4.35 million soms. The state's losses have been fully compensated.

item.title: Legal education event held for Aktobe schoolchildren on rights and law
item.description: An interactive meeting titled 'New Constitution: New Perspective, New Responsibility' was held at School No. 14 in Aktobe. The event, part of the 'Adolescent and Law' ten-day prevention campaign, aimed to explain the core values of the Constitution and prevent juvenile delinquency. Police captain Yerkeulan Kenes spoke about citizens' rights and duties.

item.title: Putin rejects Ukraine ceasefire after Crimea bridge attacks, vows 'painful' response
item.description: Russian President Vladimir Putin has reportedly abandoned the idea of a ceasefire with Ukraine following attacks on the Crimean bridge. Putin stated that Russia's response to the attacks would be 'quite painful'. The article links to further details on the Daryo.uz website.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Tax Service Head and Kazakhstan Ambassador Discuss Tax Digitalization
item.description: The head of Kyrgyzstan's Tax Service, Almamet Shykmahamatov, met with Kazakhstan's Ambassador, Abylkair Skakov, to explore cooperation in tax administration and digital technology. Both sides emphasized exchanging experiences and applying modern technologies. They agreed to continue collaboration and hold working consultations on tax administration solutions.

item.title: International Court of Justice Rules Myanmar Committed Genocide Against Rohingya
item.description: The International Court of Justice has ruled that Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya Muslim minority. The court ordered safe return and reparations for refugees. This is the first time in the court's 80-year history that it has found a country guilty of genocide, citing systematic destruction and violence.

item.title: Marat Kozhaev Elected Chairman of CIS Parliamentary Assembly's Political Affairs Commission
item.description: Marat Kozhaev has been elected as the Chairman of the Standing Commission on Political Affairs and International Cooperation of the CIS Parliamentary Assembly. The decision was made during a commission meeting in Turkmenistan. Members also heard information on Turkmenistan's upcoming CIS chairmanship and supported its request for observer status.

item.title: Kazakhstan President Tokayev Discusses Diplomacy and AI with Inter-Parliamentary Union Head
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev of Kazakhstan met with Milton Dick, President of the Inter-Parliamentary Union and Speaker of the Australian House of Representatives. They discussed parliamentary diplomacy, artificial intelligence development, and cooperation prospects with Australia. Tokayev highlighted Kazakhstan's ongoing political reforms aimed at strengthening democratic institutions.

item.title: Uzbekistan Central Bank Enhances Security for Mobile Banking and Transfers
item.description: Uzbekistan's Central Bank has introduced new rules for banks and payment organizations to combat fraud in mobile financial services. New users will undergo phone number ownership verification. Access from new devices will require biometric identification, and large transfers will need additional confirmation. Transfers between cards via websites are now prohibited, only through mobile apps.

item.title: UN University Institute to Open in Almaty, Kazakhstan
item.description: An agreement was signed between the Government of Kazakhstan and the UN University to establish a Regional Comparative Research Institute in Almaty. The institute's headquarters will be located in Almaty, fulfilling a directive from President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev. This initiative aims to strengthen UN-Kazakhstan cooperation and enhance Almaty's status as an academic hub.
